steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The first three Radeon Instinct products were announced on December 12, 2016 and they were released on June 20, 2017. Each of them was based on a different architecture.

### MI6

The MI6 is a card based on Polaris 10 and it is passively cooled. It has 16 GB of GDDR5 memory and a TDP of <150 W. It does 5.7 TFLOPS (FP16 and FP32), so it is expected to be used mainly for inference and not for neural network training. Its peak double precision (FP64) compute performance is 358 GFLOPS.

### MI8

The MI8 is a card based on Fiji, and it is analogous to the R9 Nano. It has a TDP of <175W. It has 4 GB of High Bandwidth Memory. It does 8.2 TFLOPS (FP16 and FP32), so it is marketed toward inference. Its peak double precision (FP64) compute performance is 512 GFLOPS.

### MI25

The MI25 is a card based on Vega and it uses HBM2 memory. Its performance is expected to be 12.3 TFLOPS with FP32 numbers. The MI6 and MI8 can't do this, but the MI25 can get more performance when it uses lower precision numbers, so it is expected to reach 24.6 TFLOPS with FP16 numbers. It is rated at a TDP of <300W and it is passively cooled. It also gives 768 GFLOPS of peak double precision (FP64), at 1/16th rate.

### MI50, MI60

The MI50 and MI60 are based on the Vega20 variant of GCN 5. They support FP64 at 1/2 rate. They are the last Instinct cards that have the Radeon branding, and also the last ones that can produce display output.

### MI100 series (CDNA 1)

- removed all rendering-related resources, added matrix processing units

### MI300 series

- MI300A, MI300X: data center, CDNA 3, HPC + generative AI; scalable chiplet design, TSMC CoWoS / InFO, one interposer; Infinity Fabric between chiplets and host
- MI300A: APU, 24 Zen 4 CPU cores + four CDNA 3 GPU cores, 228 CUs, 128 GB HBM3; Zen 4 on 5 nm, x86-64, AVX-512, BFloat16; 61.3 TFLOPS FP64 (122.6 matrix), 980.6 TFLOPS FP16 (1961.2 sparsity), 5.3 TB/s; PCIe 5.0, CXL 2.0
- MI300X: dedicated generative AI accelerator, CPU cores -> more GPU cores + HBM; 304 CUs (64 cores per CU), 192 GB HBM3; NLP, computer vision, deep learning; 653.7 TFLOPS TP32 (1307.4 sparsity), 1307.4 TFLOPS FP16 (2614.9 sparsity), 5.3 TB/s; PCIe 5.0, CXL 2.0, ROCm

### MI350 series

- MI350X, MI355X: CDNA 4, AI training and inference; TSMC 3 nm (N3); chiplets; 288 GB HBM3E, 8 TB/s
- native FP4, FP6 + FP8, FP16; FP4 up to 9.2 PetaFLOPS on MI355X
- Infinity Fabric kept; builds on CDNA 3; scalability, energy efficiency
- 2026: MI350P PCIe card, ~half compute and power of MI350X

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The first three Radeon Instinct products were announced on December 12, 2016 and they were released on June 20, 2017. Each of them was based on a different architecture.

### MI6

The MI6 is a card based on Polaris 10 and it is passively cooled. It has 16 GB of GDDR5 memory and a TDP of <150 W. It does 5.7 TFLOPS (FP16 and FP32), so it is expected to be used mainly for inference and not for neural network training. Its peak double precision (FP64) compute performance is 358 GFLOPS.

### MI8

The MI8 is a card based on Fiji, and it is analogous to the R9 Nano. It has a TDP of <175W. It has 4 GB of High Bandwidth Memory. It does 8.2 TFLOPS (FP16 and FP32), so it is marketed toward inference. Its peak double precision (FP64) compute performance is 512 GFLOPS.

### MI25

The MI25 is a card based on Vega and it uses HBM2 memory. Its performance is expected to be 12.3 TFLOPS with FP32 numbers. The MI6 and MI8 can't do this, but the MI25 can get more performance when it uses lower precision numbers, so it is expected to reach 24.6 TFLOPS with FP16 numbers. It is rated at a TDP of <300W and it is passively cooled. It also gives 768 GFLOPS of peak double precision (FP64), at 1/16th rate.

### MI50, MI60

The MI50 and MI60 are based on the Vega20 variant of GCN 5. They support FP64 at 1/2 rate. They are the last Instinct cards that have the Radeon branding, and also the last ones that can produce display output.

### MI100 series (CDNA 1)

The CDNA1 cards removed all of the resources related to rendering, and they added matrix processing units.

### MI300 series

The MI300A and MI300X are accelerators for the data center. They use the CDNA 3 architecture, which is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) and for generative artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. CDNA 3 has a scalable chiplet design. It uses TSMC's advanced packaging technologies, like CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) and InFO (integrated fan-out), to put multiple chiplets together on a single interposer. The chiplets are connected by AMD's Infinity Fabric, which gives high-speed and low-latency data transfer between the chiplets and the host system.

The MI300A is an accelerated processing unit (APU). It integrates 24 Zen 4 CPU cores and four CDNA 3 GPU cores, which gives a total of 228 CUs in the GPU part, and it has 128 GB of HBM3 memory. The Zen 4 CPU cores are on the 5 nm process node and they support the x86-64 instruction set, and also AVX-512 and BFloat16 extensions. The CPU cores can run general-purpose applications and they also do host-side computation for the GPU cores. The peak performance of the MI300A is 61.3 TFLOPS of FP64 (122.6 TFLOPS FP64 matrix) and 980.6 TFLOPS of FP16 (1961.2 TFLOPS with sparsity), and it has 5.3 TB/s of memory bandwidth. It supports PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0 interfaces, so it can communicate with other devices and accelerators in a heterogeneous system.

The MI300X is a dedicated generative AI accelerator. It replaces the CPU cores with more GPU cores and more HBM memory, so it has a total of 304 CUs (64 cores per CU) and 192 GB of HBM3 memory. The MI300X is designed for accelerating generative AI applications, for example natural language processing, computer vision, and deep learning. Its peak performance is 653.7 TFLOPS of TP32 (1307.4 TFLOPS with sparsity) and 1307.4 TFLOPS of FP16 (2614.9 TFLOPS with sparsity), and it has 5.3 TB/s of memory bandwidth. The MI300X also supports PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0 interfaces, and AMD's ROCm software stack, which gives a unified programming model and tools for developing and deploying generative AI applications on AMD hardware.

### MI350 series

The MI350X and MI355X are accelerators for the data center that are built on the CDNA 4 architecture, and they target advanced AI training and inference workloads. They are made on TSMC's 3 nm (N3) process, they have a high-performance chiplet design, and they have 288 GB of HBM3E memory with 8 TB/s of bandwidth. CDNA 4 adds native support for the low-precision formats FP4 and FP6, as well as FP8 and FP16, and this boosts FP4 compute to up to 9.2 PetaFLOPS on the MI355X. The architecture still uses AMD's Infinity Fabric interconnect for high-speed, low-latency data transit between the GPU chiplets and the host system. The design builds on CDNA 3 and it improves both scalability and energy efficiency for large-scale AI deployments. In 2026 AMD released the MI350P, which is a PCIe card with about half the compute capacity and power requirements of the MI350X.

### MI6

It has a peak double precision (FP64) compute performance of 358 GFLOPS.[5]

### MI8

The MI8 is a Fiji based card, analogous to the R9 Nano, with a <175W TDP.[3] The MI8 has 4 GB of High Bandwidth Memory. At 8.2 TFLOPS (FP16 and FP32), the MI8 is marketed toward inference. It has a peak double precision (FP64) compute performance of 512 GFLOPS.[6]

### MI25

The MI25 is a Vega based card that uses HBM2 memory. Its performance is expected to be 12.3 TFLOPS using FP32 numbers. Unlike the MI6 and MI8, the MI25 can increase performance when using lower precision numbers, and so is expected to reach 24.6 TFLOPS when using FP16 numbers. The MI25 is rated at <300W TDP with passive cooling. It also provides 768 GFLOPS peak double precision (FP64) at 1/16th rate.[7]

### MI50, MI60

The MI50 and MI60 are based on the Vega20 variant of GCN 5. They support 1/2 rate FP64 and are the last Instinct cards to carry the Radeon branding and the ability to produce display output.

### MI100 series (CDNA 1)

The CDNA1 cards removed all rendering-related resources and added matrix processing units.

### MI300 series

The MI300A and MI300X are data center accelerators using the CDNA 3 architecture, which is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) and generative artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. CDNA 3 has a scalable chiplet design that uses TSMC's advanced packaging technologies, such as CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) and InFO (integrated fan-out), to combine multiple chiplets on a single interposer. The chiplets are interconnected by AMD's Infinity Fabric, which enables high-speed, low-latency data transfer between the chiplets and the host system.

The MI300A is an accelerated processing unit (APU) integrating 24 Zen 4 CPU cores with four CDNA 3 GPU cores, for a total of 228 CUs in the GPU section, and 128 GB of HBM3 memory. The Zen 4 CPU cores are based on the 5 nm process node and support the x86-64 instruction set as well as AVX-512 and BFloat16 extensions. They can run general-purpose applications and provide host-side computation for the GPU cores. The MI300A has a peak performance of 61.3 TFLOPS of FP64 (122.6 TFLOPS FP64 matrix) and 980.6 TFLOPS of FP16 (1961.2 TFLOPS with sparsity), along with 5.3 TB/s of memory bandwidth. It supports PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0 interfaces, allowing it to communicate with other devices and accelerators in a heterogeneous system.

The MI300X is a dedicated generative AI accelerator that replaces the CPU cores with additional GPU cores and HBM memory, for a total of 304 CUs (64 cores per CU) and 192 GB of HBM3 memory. It is designed to accelerate generative AI applications such as natural language processing, computer vision, and deep learning. The MI300X has a peak performance of 653.7 TFLOPS of TP32 (1307.4 TFLOPS with sparsity) and 1307.4 TFLOPS of FP16 (2614.9 TFLOPS with sparsity), along with 5.3 TB/s of memory bandwidth. It also supports PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0 interfaces, as well as AMD's ROCm software stack, which provides a unified programming model and tools for developing and deploying generative AI applications on AMD hardware.[8,9,10]

### MI350 series

The MI350X and MI355X are data center accelerators built on the CDNA 4 architecture and aimed at advanced AI training and inference workloads. Manufactured on TSMC's 3 nm (N3) process, they use a high-performance chiplet design and have 288 GB of HBM3E memory with 8 TB/s of bandwidth.[11] CDNA 4 introduces native support for the low-precision formats FP4 and FP6, in addition to FP8 and FP16, boosting FP4 compute to up to 9.2 PetaFLOPS on the MI355X.[12] The architecture keeps AMD's Infinity Fabric interconnect for high-speed, low-latency data transit between GPU chiplets and the host system. The design builds on CDNA 3, advancing both scalability and energy efficiency for large-scale AI deployments. In 2026, AMD released the MI350P, a PCIe card with roughly half the compute capacity and power requirements of the MI350X.
